extracted.intended_audience: inventors, applicants and patent agents seeking to file a patent application in Singapore via the domestic route
extracted.subtask_description: Step-by-step guidance for filing and prosecuting a patent application directly in Singapore via the domestic route, covering required documents, preliminary examination, publication, search & examination route choices, responses to examination, grant formalities, timelines, fees and renewal obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application contents (required documents)
rubrics_metrics.description: Your patent application must include: Application form; Description of the invention, with at least one way of carrying out the invention claimed; drawings, if any (in black & white or grayscale); Claims, if ready; Abstract of the invention; Application fee of S$170/-.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may file your patent application online via the IPOS Digital Hub. If the claims are not fully ready at the point of filing and you wish to secure an early filing date, consider filing a provisional application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional application option
rubrics_metrics.description: If the claims are not fully ready at the point of filing the patent application and you wish to secure an early filing date for your invention, you may consider filing a provisional application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A provisional application can be used to secure an early filing date while finalising claims; see the 'Provisional Application' guidance page for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Date of Filing and deficiency notification
rubrics_metrics.description: Once the filing requirements are met, the Registry of Patents will accord a Date of Filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If filing requirements are not met, you will be notified by the Registrar to provide what is lacking within 2 months. The application will be treated as abandoned if you cannot submit the necessary items in time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary examination trigger conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Registrar will proceed to conduct a preliminary examination on your application when the filing fee is paid and claims are submitted within the specified time periods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page notes specific time limits for payment and claims (see separate metrics). Preliminary examination is a formal check before substantive search/examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary examination checks
rubrics_metrics.description: The preliminary examination ensures that: the priority claim is correct; there are no missing drawings or parts of description; and the application complies with all formal requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are formal compliance checks; failure to meet them triggers notification to amend (see next metric).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of failing preliminary examination requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: If the preliminary examination requirements are not complied with, you will be notified by the Registrar to amend the application within 2 months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to amend within the 2-month period will result in your application being refused.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing fee payment deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: Filing fee is to be paid within 1 month from filing the patent application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The application form lists an Application fee of S$170/-; other search/examination fees apply at later stages (see search/examination routes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims filing deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims are to be filed within 12 months from priority date or filing date, whichever is earlier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submitting claims within this period is necessary for the Registrar to proceed with preliminary examination and to preserve rights based on priority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication timing and options
rubrics_metrics.description: Details of your patent application will be published in the Patents Journal as soon as possible after 18 months from declared priority date or, where there is no declared priority date, the date of filing of the patent application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may request early publication (for example, where you wish to have your patent granted in less than 18 months). If you wish to keep your invention secret, do not proceed with the application; you may withdraw your application earlier than one month before expiry of the 18 months. Once the application is granted you may be able to take action for infringement and seek damages that occur from the date of publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search and examination substantive purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent examiners will search for similar earlier inventions (prior art) and examine and compare the prior art to determine if the prior art destroys the novelty of your patent application and whether other patentability criteria (such as inventive step and industrial application) are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the substantive assessment of registrability (novelty, inventive step, industrial applicability).

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice of search and examination route (Options 1–3)
rubrics_metrics.description: You can choose any of the 3 search and examination routes depending on the availability of foreign search and/or examination results and cost.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Option details provided: Option 1 — Search within 13 months + Examination within 36 months; Fees: Search (S$1,735) + Examination (S$1,420); Advantage: opportunity to decide whether to proceed with examination depending on search results; Disadvantage: more expensive than Option 2 if proceeding with examination. Option 2 — Combined search and examination within 36 months; Fee: S$2,050; Advantage: enjoy time and cost savings compared to Option 1. Option 3 — Examination within 36 months; Fee: S$1,420; Advantage: less expensive if a foreign search result is available; Disadvantage: there may be other prior arts not uncovered in earlier search.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee discounts and excess claim fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Fee discount and excess claim fees may apply for the different options.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 'Forms and fees for new applications' for details on discounts and additional claim fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Work-sharing arrangements (PPH, ASPEC) usage
rubrics_metrics.description: If you have foreign search and examination results from partnering offices, you can make use of work-sharing arrangements such as Patent Prosecution Highway (PPH) and ASEAN Patent Examination Cooperation (ASPEC) Programme to obtain a patent in Singapore faster and more efficiently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using partner office results can reduce cost and time; eligibility and procedures are subject to the respective programmes' rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination report outcomes and response options
rubrics_metrics.description: After the search and examination process, an examination report will be issued detailing the patent examiners’ opinion on registrability. If there are no unresolved objections you will be issued a Notice of Eligibility to Proceed to Grant. If there are one or more unresolved objections you are required to respond within 2 months (for simple amendment via invitation to amend) or 5 months (for written opinion).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permitted responses include: written submissions on the examiner's opinion; an amendment of the patent specification; rejection of the invitation to amend (with or without explanation); or all of the above. Subsequent written opinion(s) may be issued until all outstanding issues are resolved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of Intention to Refuse timing
rubrics_metrics.description: If the outstanding issues cannot be resolved within 18 months from the date of the first written opinion, you will receive a Notice of Intention to Refuse from the Registry of Patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This sets a firm outer limit for resolving substantive objections arising from examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for issuance of Certificate of Grant and consolidated specification
rubrics_metrics.description: You must file a request for the issuance of the Certificate of Grant within 2 months after receiving the Notice of Eligibility to Proceed to Grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you have made any amendments or corrections to the original specification, you need to submit a set of consolidated specification together with the request for the issuance of the Certificate of Grant. If the request is filed and conditions for grant are satisfied, the Registrar will issue the Certificate of Grant. If you fail to file the request, the patent application shall be treated as abandoned and the Registrar will notify you accordingly by letter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent term and renewal obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Once your patent is granted, it will be protected for 20 years from the Date of Filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The patent is to be renewed yearly, starting from its 5th year.
